context.passage:
Hanson Press A nnounces
A cquisition

LONDON (6 September)-Publishing
giant Hanson Press yesterday announced
that it had successfully acquired Cassidy
Books, a well-regarded publisher of trade
books. While Hanson has been a force in
university textbook publishing for more
than 25 years, its latest expansion is
expected to solidify its presence in the
general readership market.

Over the past five years, Hanson acquired
British trade book publishers Wingate
Press and Pelagornis Publishing.
However, the addition of Cassidy Books
holds special significance. "Cassidy has a

huge market in the United States and a
large presence in Canada," said Hanson's
CEO, Ravinder Kachru. "Not only will
this give us a foothold in North A merica,
it will also increase our visibility as an
academic publisher."

A mongst Cassidy's most notable titles is
Spencer Blackhorse's bestselling memoir
Whispers, which chronicles his childhood
in a remote part of A laska. Cassidy has
also discovered emerging talents like
Shannon Oliver, known for her gripping
thrillers, and romance novelist Lilli Gu.
